title: The economy breathes in and out
hook: Why can't the good times just keep going forever?
metaphor: Borrowing is like a breath in. You get more to spend today. Paying it back is the breath out, and you spend less for a while.
body: Cheap loans let people and companies spend more than they earn.
That extra spending is somebody else's income, so everything speeds up.
Eventually the loans must be paid back, and spending slows.
This runs roughly every five to seven years. That is the cycle.

live.template: The engine reads the economy as {needle} right now, and it has looked that way since {since}.

caveat: Cycles do not run on a timetable. Five to seven years is an average, not a schedule.
